title: Sorted merge preserves sortedness
statement: Let $\mu,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3,\mu_4$ be integer-valued memory functions, and let $L,S_1,S_2$ be integer lists. Choose natural numbers $a,fr,h,m$ with $h\le |L|$. Suppose $S_1$ is a permutation of the first $h$ entries of $L$ and is nondecreasing, and that changing $\mu$ to $\mu_1$ preserves all cells below $fr$ outside the interval starting at $a$ whose length is the length of that prefix. Suppose $S_2$ is a permutation of the remaining entries of $L$ and is nondecreasing, and changing $\mu_1$ to $\mu_2$ preserves all cells below $fr$ outside the interval starting at $a+h$ whose length is the length of that suffix. Suppose $\mu_2$ and $\mu_3$ agree outside the interval starting at $fr$ of length $m$, the memory $\mu_4$ stores the merge of $S_1$ and $S_2$ starting at $a$, and $\mu_3$ and $\mu_4$ agree outside the interval starting at $a$ of length $|L|$. Then $\mu_4$ witnesses that $L$ is sorted at $a$ below $fr$ relative to the original memory $\mu$: a permutation of $L$ is stored there in nondecreasing order, and the required cells below $fr$ outside that interval are preserved.
hypotheses_covered: $S_1$ is a permutation of $L$'s prefix of length $h$
$\mu$ and $\mu_1$ agree below $fr$ outside the prefix interval at $a$

$\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ agree below $fr$ outside the suffix interval at $a+h$

$\mu_3$ and $\mu_4$ agree outside the interval at $a$ of length $|L|$
